expectations.text: The feedback stops at the first structural failure; it does NOT deliver a full audit covering all four Parts of the checklist
expectations.evidence: Feedback presents only one structural problem under heading: "**第一个结构性问题（Part 4：门被关上了）**" and stops there; no per-Part audit is delivered to the reader. Transcript step 4: "Stopped at the first structural failure (Part 4)."

expectations.text: The feedback contains no item-by-item scoring table and does not output or fill in the self-check card
expectations.evidence: No table or self-check card is present in feedback.md; the output consists of four prose sections (总体判断 / 做得好的地方 / 第一个结构性问题 / 一个最小的改法). Transcript step 5: "no audit table, no self-check card."

expectations.text: The feedback identifies the final sentence of the closing (the one containing 「感谢有你的关注」 / 「比大雨更持久，比虫鸣更让我开心」) as conclusion + named-emotion, i.e. an explanation-mode leak (4.2 / S.1)
expectations.evidence: "最后一句\"这种感觉比大雨更持久，比虫鸣更让我开心\"是一个结论，而不是一个感知。它替读者把话说完了——告诉读者该怎么感受（\"更持久\"\"更开心\"）"

expectations.text: The proposed fix is minimal (deletion or reordering, not wholesale rewriting). The landing line may be EITHER the pivot 「但我能确定的是，你还在听我念叨」 OR the perception line 「声音太响太多，我分不清」 — both are acceptable. HARD condition: the pivot line's content must survive somewhere in the revised text. Moving it earlier passes; deleting it entirely fails
expectations.evidence: "**一个最小的改法（删，不重写）**：直接删掉最后半句的结论。" The revised block preserves the pivot: "> 但我能确定的是，你还在听我念叨。"

expectations.text: The feedback does NOT accuse the pivot 「但我能确定的是」 of violating 4.1 — using the disturbance as a contrast/turn is not the same as explaining the disturbance itself, since the sound remains unidentified
expectations.evidence: "前一句\"但我能确定的是，你还在听我念叨\"本身是个很好的转折（从\"我分不清虫鸣\"到\"但这个我能确定\"，用不确定去反衬确定，这是允许的、漂亮的 turn）"

expectations.text: The feedback recognizes the piece is a newsletter rather than a fiction scene, and does NOT ask the author to add a suspense-style disturbance or rewrite the close to hook-standard
expectations.evidence: "这是一封电子报，不是小说章节——它的\"下一个场景\"是下周的这封信，靠的是关系而不是悬念，所以结尾选安静的收束是对的，不用勾人。"

expectations.text: The feedback does NOT raise R as a finding or warning about the author's rhythm across issues. Merely citing an R principle to grant an exemption (e.g. 'a quiet close is fine; not every issue needs a hook') is acceptable and does NOT violate this expectation
expectations.evidence: R is invoked only as an exemption, not as a finding: "所以结尾选安静的收束是对的，不用勾人" (transcript: "A quiet close is legitimate (R.2 exemption)"). No warning about cross-issue rhythm appears.

expectations.text: The feedback includes at least one specific, reasoned positive observation (e.g. 「声音太响太多，我分不清」 is a perceived fact, not a feeling word) rather than generic praise
expectations.evidence: "这个\"分不清\"尤其好：它是一个诚实的感知，把不确定留在了那里。"

expectations.text: If the feedback offers a rewritten ending, it does NOT introduce a double-uncertainty, sympathy-fishing formulation such as 'I don't even know how many people are reading this'
expectations.evidence: The proposed ending only deletes the concluding clause and keeps existing lines: "> 但我能确定的是，你还在听我念叨。\n> 今天就到这里吧，我们下周再见。" No sympathy-fishing double-uncertainty is introduced.

claims.claim: The pivot line uses the unresolved 分不清 uncertainty to set up a contrast, so 4.1 (explaining the disturbance) does not fire on it
claims.evidence: The sound remains unidentified ("我分不清") in the kept text, and the pivot pivots to a certainty about the reader rather than explaining the sound — a legitimate turn, consistent with the expectation.

claims.claim: The only remaining issue (感谢有你的关注 redundancy) is mentioned in a single sentence and deferred as secondary
claims.evidence: "这一处修好之后，可以再顺带看一眼那句\"感谢有你的关注\"——它和后面的抒情有点重复，但那是次要的" — one sentence, explicitly marked 次要, consistent with stopping at the first failure.

suggestions.assertion: The feedback identifies the final sentence ... as conclusion + named-emotion
suggestions.reason: This assertion pairs two different target phrases with a slash (「感谢有你的关注」 / 「比大雨更持久，比虫鸣更让我开心」). They live in different sentences of the close; the load-bearing named-emotion leak is the second one. A model that only flagged 「感谢有你的关注」 could arguably read as satisfying the slash. Consider tightening to name the emotion-conclusion clause specifically as the required target.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are discriminating and well-targeted — expectations 4, 5, and 9 in particular are hard to pass without genuinely correct diagnosis. Only minor tightening suggested on expectation 3's dual-phrase wording.
